description: Horizontal levels 1-10 tickers actually reacted at, nearest to spot first, each with its touch, break and flip history. Use it to place a stop or a target. It reports where price turned before, not whether it is turning now. Analyst plan.

include_series.description: Include the [unix_seconds, open, high, low, close] bars the map was built on — up to ~1750 rows per ticker on the hourly ranges. Default false.

range.description: Window to map. 2y (the default) and 5y are daily-bar maps — the readable lens for 'where are this name's levels'. 6mo and 1y are hourly-bar maps of recent structure: finer granularity, many more zones, use them when you want the near-term map rather than the chart-reader's one.

tickers.description: Comma-separated tickers, e.g. 'MSFT,NVDA'. Required; at most 10 per call, each at most 12 characters: the exchange ticker, with a venue suffix for a non-US listing (BRK-B, RHM.DE, SAP.DE); FX as the 6-letter pair (EURUSD), indices by short code (SPX). Futures whose code is also a US listing go by their contract root behind a slash, the broker convention — /CL (WTI crude), /HG, /PL, /NG, /RB, /HO; coins by their USD pair (BTCUSD, ETHUSD); the MOVE index as MOVEINDEX; the bare code (WTI, HG, BTC…) means the listing.

top.description: Levels kept per ticker, nearest to spot first. Default scales with the ticker count so the response stays inside the client token budget: 12 for one ticker, 6 for two, 4 for three, 3 from four up. `count` always reports how many were found.
